svg.text: Teryx OS wiring, sheet 'winch'. Made from config/wiring.yaml by `python -m teryx wiring`. Don't edit this file.
Labels: wire id, size, fuse (if the wire has its own), and anything in between. Faded = optional. Hover for notes. Full table: docs/wiring/README.md

g.title: WN01: BAT12.pos -> BRK_WINCH.in - Cable that came with the winch
WN06: WINCH_SOL.REMOTE -> WINCH_REMOTE.PLUG - XBull remote stays as a backup
WN10: RELAYS.NO4 -> WINCH_SOL.COIL_IN - winch.in. Never the motor current through the relay board
WN11: RELAYS.NO5 -> WINCH_SOL.COIL_OUT - winch.out, interlocked with in
WN19: WINCH_SOL.COIL_IN -> WINCH_SOL.GND - Across the coil, at the solenoid box, unless the box already has one. Stops the coil's kick arcing the relay contacts and spiking the 12 V
WN21: WINCH_SOL.REM_IN -> WINCH_SOL.COIL_IN - Inside the solenoid box: cut the remote socket's in wire off the coil and rejoin it through this diode
BAT12: 12 V aux battery - Kept after the conversion. Charged by the DC-DC

BRK_WINCH: 250 A breaker - Manual reset breaker, also the winch's kill switch: push it off to make the winch dead. No isolator contactor (Sam, 18 Nov), so the XBull remote and hand switches work whenever this is on

WINCH_SOL: XBull solenoid box - The remote socket's in and out lines are cut from the coils inside the box and rejoined through their own diodes (WN21, WN22), like the hand switches. Then the in.winch_remote tap sees only the remote, not the Pico's own relays 4-5 driving the coils (found by the system sim, 23 Nov: tapped at the coil, the Pico would stop its own winch pull)

RELAYS: 16-ch relay board, channels 1-8 - One 16-channel board of mechanical 5 V relays with opto and JD-VCC jumper (AliExpress cart), in an aux box next to the control box. RELAYS2 is channels 9-16 of the same board. The solid state G3MB-202P board Sam has is AC only and won't turn off on 12 V DC. JD-VCC jumper off, coils on 5 V, inputs from 3.3 V
HSW_WINCH: Hidden winch switch (at the winch) - Momentary (ON)-OFF-(ON)
HSW_CAB: Hidden winch switch (in the cab) - Momentary (ON)-OFF-(ON)

FB: Blade fuse block - 12 fuses in use. Small loads that can go out together share a fuse (front bars in pairs, trailer tail + stop, interior bar + accessory). All four front bars are NOT on one fuse, so one fault can't black out the front at night. The winch, control box power, key, power hold and each actuator keep their own. Sam's 12-way (in the post) is used, so it is full with no spares; add a small 6-way next to it if more circuits come
